title: Ines and the Wolf
premise: Orsen Villalobos, a scribe bound by debt to the Guild of Impossible Things, discovers that the ledgers he keeps record not goods but souls — including one belonging to Ines, a wolf-gifted girl the guild sold to the court beneath the mountain. When the crown declares a hunt for all gifted people, Orsen's own hidden gift marks him as prey, forcing him to flee with a ragged found family of hunted strangers. To free Ines before her soul is consumed to feed the mountain court's immortality, Orsen must trade his own memories of everyone he loves. He does so, saving Ines and breaking the guild's power, and though he no longer remembers them, they choose to remember him — teaching him who he was, one story at a time.
about_author: Xanthe Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing debts in old merchant houses before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paper trails, quiet crimes, and the people who survive both.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. In the guildhall at Vellamarch, Orsen balances accounts for impossible trades — a shadow pawned, a name sold twice. He hides his own gift: ink that moves when he writes true things. Emotional beat: weary complicity; he tells himself the ledger only records, never causes.

chapters.title: A Girl with Winter in Her Teeth
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. A debt-bound girl named Ines arrives as collateral, wolf-gifted and half-feral, and Orsen is ordered to catalogue her soul for sale. He falsifies an entry to buy her time. Emotional beat: first crack in his neutrality — guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Crown's Proclamation
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Heralds announce a kingdom-wide hunt for the gifted; guildmasters begin selling their own debtors to the crown for protection. Orsen learns Ines has already been sold onward — to the court beneath the mountain. Emotional beat: dread; the machinery he served now hunts him too.

chapters.title: What the Ink Confessed
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. His moving ink betrays him during inspection; a sympathetic clerk, Maren, burns the evidence and flees with him through the flooded archive tunnels. Emotional beat: terror and improbable relief — the first bond of the found family forming under pressure.

chapters.title: The Road of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: POV Orsen and Maren alternating. On the road, they gather other hunted strays: Tobin, a boy who hears doors before they open, and Sefa, an aging hedge-witch. Emotional beat: cautious warmth; strangers learning to sleep in shifts, watch for each other.

chapters.title: The Wolf That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: POV Maren. The group finds traces of Ines's transport — a slaughtered escort, chains torn like paper. Something wolf-shaped is following them through the pines. Emotional beat: hope tangled with fear; is it Ines escaped, or the thing she became?

chapters.title: Bargain at the Tollhouse
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. A crown tollhouse demands papers they don't have; Orsen trades a memory of his mother to a memory-broker for forged documents. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal — he can no longer recall her face.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: POV Tobin. From a ridge, they see the mountain city where the court buys souls to extend its own. Tobin's door-hearing gift maps its sealed ways. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror at the scale of what feeds on the gifted.

chapters.title: Ines, Running
chapters.summary: POV Ines (first appearance). Inside the mountain, Ines endures the soul-tithe rituals, holding onto herself by remembering the guildhall, the scribe who lied in the ledger to protect her. Emotional beat: ferocious endurance; she refuses to forget who she is.

chapters.title: The Broker's Price
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. The memory-broker reappears with an offer: passage into the mountain in exchange for Orsen's memories of his found family — the only currency the court's gatekeepers accept from the gifted. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; survival priced against love.

chapters.title: Doors That Listen
chapters.summary: POV Tobin. Tobin guides them through the mountain's servant ways, hearing each door's mood. Sefa nearly dies sealing a ward behind them. Emotional beat: trust deepening into family; each member covering another's weakness.

chapters.title: The Tithe Hall
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Ines witnesses the tithe ceremony — a gifted child emptied entirely, smiling as they fade. She resolves to escape or die whole. Emotional beat: grief and defiance; the stakes become unbearably personal.

chapters.title: Ledger-Keeper, Thief
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Orsen infiltrates the court's record-vaults, discovering his own guild founded the tithe system — and that his debt was engineered to keep him writing. Emotional beat: betrayal; his whole life reframed as someone else's transaction.

chapters.title: The Shape of Her Name
chapters.summary: POV Orsen and Ines. Orsen finds Ines mid-transfer; their reunion is interrupted by the court's Soulwarden. Ines, half-wolfed, recognizes him anyway. Emotional beat: fierce joy cut short — captured together, separated again.

chapters.title: The Warden's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. The Soulwarden offers Orsen his freedom and erased debt if he surrenders Ines's soul-contract willingly. He pretends to consider while copying the vault's master key in moving ink. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the scribe becomes the thief.

chapters.title: Everything I Priced
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. To open the vault, Orsen pays the broker fully — surrendering every memory of Maren, Tobin, Sefa, and Ines. He completes the theft knowing he won't know why it mattered. Emotional beat: devastating sacrifice performed calmly, which makes it worse.

chapters.title: The Mountain Wakes
chapters.summary: POV ensemble. The stolen contracts burn; the court's stored souls erupt. Maren, Tobin, and Sefa fight through collapsing galleries to reach the vault. Emotional beat: chaos and courage; the family fighting for a man who no longer knows them.

chapters.title: Wolf at the Heart
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Ines, contract destroyed, fully takes her wolf shape and tears the Soulwarden's tithe-engine apart. She carries the blank-eyed Orsen out as the mountain caves. Emotional beat: triumphant fury softening into tenderness toward a stranger who saved her.

chapters.title: Ash and Ledger Paper
chapters.summary: POV Maren. The survivors regroup outside; the guild's power collapses as its records burn across the kingdom. Orsen wakes knowing nothing of any of them. Emotional beat: hollow victory; freedom purchased with someone's entire past.

chapters.title: Strangers Who Stay
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Orsen confronts the strangers who claim to be his family, suspicious and grieving something he can't name. Ines shows him his own handwriting in the burned ledger fragment — proof he chose this. Emotional beat: fragile acceptance; choosing to trust the evidence of love.

chapters.title: The Reckoning of Debts
chapters.summary: POV ensemble. The group dismantles the remaining tithe houses, freeing the hollowed and reuniting them with fragments brokers still hold. Orsen begins keeping a new ledger: not debts owed, but stories told. Emotional beat: purpose rebuilt from ruin.

chapters.title: Ines and the Wolf
chapters.summary: POV Ines and Orsen. By winter fire, the family retells Orsen his own life, one night at a time. Ines promises to be his memory until the stories take root. Some faces return; some never do. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace — survival's price paid, but love, freely given, refusing to stay forgotten.
